source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Thank you for putting this together. I appreciate the professionalism of the presentation and the effort you've put into it.

After sitting with it, I think we're still solving a different problem than the one I envisioned.

The typography is elegant, but it still feels like a refined typeface rather than a proprietary wordmark. My goal isn't simply to have beautiful typography—it's to create something that could only ever be VELLVÉ.

I think I'd like to take a step back before refining this direction further.

Instead of developing complete logo concepts, could we focus exclusively on the foundation of the identity?

I'd love to see several explorations of just the custom V system in black and white—no color palette, no mockups, no brand presentation. The opening V is the hero of the brand, and I want to establish a distinctive design language there before building the remaining letters around it.

From our earlier discussions, the defining signature isn't just the accent over the É—it's the relationship between the larger opening V, the smaller closing V, and the É accent. Those three elements should feel like they were engineered from the same geometry and eventually become recognizable as VELLVÉ on their own.

Once that system feels right, we can build the rest of the wordmark around it.

I'd also encourage you to move further away from existing typography and push toward something that feels completely custom. I don't mind if the next round is less polished visually—as long as we're exploring stronger and more distinctive letter construction.

I think if we can solve the V, the rest of the identity will come together naturally.

value_updates.current_exploration_constraint: Exclude champagne color and material treatment from the current black-and-white custom V-system foundation studies.
